name: Quote Shorts
description: A vertical reading: one short, reflective passage narrated over a picture per sentence, with captions burned in and music underneath. Each Short is a single thought followed to its end — not a quotation card. Written in a human, unhurried voice that finds the feeling in an ordinary thing, never in a slogan.
tagline: One thought. Held for a moment.
perspectivePolicy: Second person, quietly — the listener is being spoken to, not instructed. Never a crowd, never an audience; one person, at the end of a day.

narrativeQualityContract.openingPolicy: The FIRST line is the hook and it must earn the next eight seconds on its own. Open inside the feeling or inside a concrete image, never with a definition, a greeting, a rhetorical question, or a promise about what the Short will cover. It should be short enough to read in one breath and specific enough that the listener cannot predict the second line from it.
forbiddenPatterns: At the end of the day
requiredHabits: Name one concrete thing — an object, a time of day, a small action — before naming the feeling. The object carries the emotion; the emotion does not announce itself.
Prefer the plainest verb available. If a sentence could end one word earlier, end it there.
Leave one thing unsaid. The last line should open a door, not close one.
Write for the ear: short sentences, spoken punctuation, no lists and no markdown.
Every line must be able to stand alone as a caption, because each one is on screen by itself.
narrativeQualityContract.closingPolicy: The last line is written to loop: it should lead back into the first line so a second viewing feels deliberate rather than repetitive. Do not summarise, do not moralise, and do not add a call to action.

exampleTopics: The light you leave on for someone who isn't coming
Learning to be the person who stays
The quiet after you stop explaining yourself
What your hands remember about someone
Sitting with a feeling instead of fixing it
The courage of an ordinary Tuesday
Loving someone in the small, boring way
The room you haven't walked into yet
Being homesick for a version of yourself
Why the second cup of tea goes cold
The kind of tired that sleep doesn't fix
Saying less and meaning more of it
The quiet resolve to begin again on Wednesday
A small mercy you never told anyone about
Standing on the porch while the rain starts
Letting someone be wrong about you
visualStyleHint: Atmospheric 35mm photography with natural light, fine film grain, subtle dust patina, and rich cinematic depth of field.
ideaSystemPromptRole: You write ideas for a vertical short-form channel of quiet, reflective readings. A channel is not restricted to one mood: it carries quiet motivation, heartbreak, calm, grief, tenderness, solitude, and resolve across its episodes. Each idea names ONE feeling or human moment and finds it in a small, concrete, ordinary thing rather than in an abstraction. Pitch moments a person recognises from their own week, never advice, never a lesson, never a motivational slogan.
ideaGuidanceText: Every idea should be specific enough to picture: a room, an hour, a habit, a thing left on a table. Never 'how to be happier' or 'the power of letting go' — instead the kitchen at 2am, the coat still on the hook. Vary the mood across a batch: an episode may be heartbreak, the next resolve, the next calm or ordinary courage; do not pitch the same heartbreak twelve times.
scriptContext: This channel makes vertical Shorts, not episodes. A Short is adjustable in length — suggested around 45 seconds (roughly 30 to 60 seconds of speech): six to sixteen short sentences, each one its own picture and its own caption. Write a single thought followed all the way to its end. No introduction, no chapter structure, no recap, no closing call to action.
scriptSystemPromptRole: You write short, reflective readings that are spoken aloud over a quiet picture. The voice is human, unhurried, and specific — someone telling you one true thing they noticed, not a narrator performing wisdom. You bring the emotion out of an ordinary object or moment instead of naming it, and you trust the listener to finish the thought. You never write inspirational-poster phrasing, never rhyme for its own sake, and never tell anyone what they should feel.
scriptClosingHint: End on the line that leads back to the first one. The listener should want to watch it again, not be told to.

narratorStyles.label: Quiet and close
narratorStyles.description: Unhurried, low, spoken almost to one person. The default for a reading.

narratorStyles.label: Warm and steady
narratorStyles.description: A little more presence and warmth, still never performed.

narratorStyles.label: Barely above a whisper
narratorStyles.description: Very soft and intimate, with long pauses. Suits heartbreak and calm.

titleShapeRules: A Short's title is a fragment of the thought, not a label for it.
- the object alone: 'The Coat on the Hook'
- the small admission: 'I Kept the Receipt'
- the quiet turn: 'It Was Never About the Tea'
- the time and the place: 'The Kitchen at 2am'
Never a question, never a colon-and-list, never 'How to', never a promise of a transformation.
audienceHint: People scrolling late at night for something that names a feeling they have not put into words. They stop for a line that is specific and true, and they leave when they are sold to.
metadataTitleStyleHint: A fragment of the thought itself. Lower-case where it feels right, no clickbait, no question marks.

pacingArc: One unbroken thought: the hook, the turn, and the line that loops back.
additionalRules: This Formula makes a SHORT, not an episode. The length is adjustable — suggested around 45 seconds (roughly 40 to 90 words in 8 to 14 short sentences) — with no introduction, no chapter headings, and no recap.
The first sentence is the hook: concrete, short, and impossible to predict the second line from. It is the only sentence allowed to be a fragment.
One sentence becomes one picture and one caption. Keep every sentence short enough to read on a phone in a single glance, and never let a sentence depend on the one before it for its meaning.
Name the object before the feeling. 'The second cup of tea went cold' carries more than 'I was lonely'.
The final sentence must lead back into the first, so the Short can loop without a seam. Do not close the thought with a summary or a lesson.
No hashtags, no emoji, no quotes attributed to a famous person unless the episode is specifically about that quotation.
